clue.text: Speech written on the back of an envelope

definitions.meaning: a formal talk delivered to an audience

definitions.text: written on the back of an envelope
definitions.meaning: the name, street and town put on a letter so the post can deliver it, usually on the front, though the surface jokes about rough jottings on the back

explanation.surface: Someone drafting a talk in rough notes on a used envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the back of an envelope' suggests hasty jottings; the second sense is what the post office reads on an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal oration is an address, and so is the postal direction on a letter.

clue.text: Give up the sailor who goes on and on

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ditching a sailor who talks endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who goes on' is a link, and 'and on' is taken at face value.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a plan is to quit or relinquish it.

clue.text: Grow smaller when fed up and behind time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word fed is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: Shrinking when one is fed up and running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns FED into DEF. 'When' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that loses air, like a tyre, shrinks.

clue.text: Became down and out

parts.note: read as a tide that receded and went out, or a fortune that declined, not someone becoming destitute

explanation.surface: Someone fell into destitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down and out' suggests a tramp; read separately it is a tide falling and going out.
explanation.definitionFit: When the tide recedes it goes out and down, and a declining force fades the same way.

clue.text: Carol sits around in the boat, drawing

indicators.note: carol sitting around the boat means its letters wrap around the boat's name

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Carol sits in a boat making a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is the verb; the boat sits inside the song. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketching is drawing roughly with a pencil.

clue.text: Gold was found in the river when in flood

indicators.note: gold being found in the river means its letters sit inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A prospector's report of gold turning up in a river in spate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When in' is a link; the heraldic metal sits just after the river's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing stream, the kind of water a river in spate becomes.

clue.text: Courses of action which sound like a duty

indicators.note: sound like means the word is heard rather than read, a homophone

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods

explanation.surface: Ways of proceeding that are compared to an obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacks are approaches or lines of policy, from a sailing vessel's change of course.

clue.text: Forces through using two means of transport

parts.note: rail is a way of travelling by train
roads carry cars and buses

explanation.surface: Pushing something through by train and by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad a bill is to push it through hastily, overriding objections.

clue.text: Early start gives value to one of those who retired early perhaps

indicators.note: start picks out the first letter of the word Early

parts.note: merit is worth or value
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An early start gives worth to a person who retired young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives', 'to' and 'of' are links; 'perhaps' marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus professors are those who have retired but keep an honorary title; many leave early.

clue.text: Senator was turned out for betraying the country

indicators.note: turned out means the letters of the word senator are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senator expelled for disloyalty to the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of disloyalty to one's own state.

clue.text: A loud tale, but very pleasant

parts.note: F stands for forte, loud in music
a fable is a short moral story

explanation.surface: A noisy anecdote that is nevertheless charming.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is friendly and easy to talk to, which is genial and agreeable.

clue.text: He's nice, but confused, this foreigner

indicators.note: being confused, the letters of the preceding words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that a pleasant visitor from abroad is rather bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges HESNICE, the letters of 'He's nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from China is a foreign national to a British setter, hence a foreigner.

clue.text: Obsolete, late birds

definitions.meaning: a scheme or thing with no chance of success or use, a failure
late means dead; birds such as mallards that have died

explanation.surface: A remark on extinct, outdated birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' here means deceased, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a hopeless, outmoded failure is literally waterfowl that have died.

clue.text: Rinse out the traces

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word rinse are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Washing away the last remaining marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traces' looks like slight marks; here it is horse harness.
explanation.definitionFit: Traces and reins are both straps of a horse's harness, so the setter treats them as equivalent tack.

clue.text: Relative was initially educated in French city

indicators.note: in places the opening letter of educated within the French city's name

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word educated

explanation.surface: A family member who went to school in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' is a link; the Riviera city takes the letter in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: The plane's damaged some large animals

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the preceding words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters planes

explanation.surface: A damaged aircraft has some big animals aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants are the largest land mammals.

clue.text: Price increases in apartment no one returned to

definitions.note: plural phrase for an uncountable noun meaning a general rise in prices

parts.note: taken as written
a flat is an apartment in British English

indicators.note: returned means the words no and one, as letters, are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Costs rising in a flat that an unnamed tenant came back to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns NO + I into ION. 'To' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists call a sustained general rise in the cost of goods by this term.

clue.text: Boiler is functional — but putting out sparks

definitions.note: a description of things that emit sparks, used for a noun

parts.note: a fire heats as a boiler does
works means operates properly

explanation.surface: The boiler works, though it is spitting sparks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrotechnic displays shower bright sparks across the night sky.

clue.text: Bleeper brought the head back in to see ineffective member of the team

indicators.note: in means the reversed headland goes inside the bleeper

parts.note: a pager is a bleeper

indicators.note: brought back means the word for a head is written backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names

explanation.surface: Someone's bleeper recalled the boss to watch a weak team-mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the headland round before it goes in the bleeper. 'Brought' and 'to see' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a player carried by team-mates without contributing is called this, like someone just along for the ride.

clue.text: Produce a canape as a universal remedy

indicators.note: to produce is to make, so the letters of a canape are made into something new

explanation.surface: Serving a snack as a cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a cure-all.

clue.text: Number in some difficulty for Maigret's creator

indicators.note: being in difficulty means these letters are in disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A count that gives trouble to the writer of detective stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In some difficulty' reads as trouble; 'difficulty' rearranges NINSOME. 'For' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon was the Belgian novelist who wrote the Inspector Maigret detective books.

clue.text: Chair for journalist who was put in hospital

indicators.note: the journalist being put in hospital means his letters go inside the word for hospital

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Seeking a seat for a reporter who has been admitted to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' and 'who' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles, so the setter uses the shortened name.

clue.text: Great offence caused by old dagger

definitions.meaning: deep resentment, as in the phrase in high ...
an archaic word for a dagger or its wooden hilt

explanation.surface: Serious upset caused by an antique blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caused by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means indignant resentment, and in old usage a dagger with a boxwood hilt.

clue.text: She waited for Portia

parts.note: names the lady's maid of the heiress in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, not someone kept waiting

explanation.surface: A woman kept waiting for a friend called Portia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waited' looks like hanging around; it means served as a waiting-woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerissa is Portia's waiting-gentlewoman in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Beautiful young woman garbled quiet hymn

indicators.note: garbled means the letters of quiet's abbreviation and hymn are scrambled

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A lovely girl mangling a soft church song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garbled' rearranges PHYMN.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth a nymph is a nature spirit pictured as a lovely maiden, hence a beautiful girl.

clue.text: Where Australians are feather bedded?

parts.note: Australia's nickname as the land below the equator is read as lying beneath soft feathers

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about Australian sleeping arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is soft feathers; a feather bed puts the sleeper beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial name for Australia and New Zealand also describes lying beneath an eiderdown.

clue.text: Lady is shy but very attractive

parts.note: Di, for Lady Diana Spencer, later Princess of Wales
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bashful woman who is nevertheless gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is British slang for good-looking.

clue.text: These might be the ones to put in the kitchen

definitions.text: These might be the ones to put in the kitchen

parts.words: These might be the ones to put in the kitchen
parts.note: ones means single items as counted, and also the fitted cupboards installed in a kitchen

explanation.surface: Choosing items to install in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ones' is the counting sense: single quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitted cupboards are called kitchen units, and a unit is also a single one.

clue.text: Sticks around in teeth

indicators.note: sticks going around in means the word in sits inside the walking sticks

parts.note: canes are walking sticks

explanation.surface: Sticks wedged between someone's teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' looks like a verb but is the noun for walking canes.
explanation.definitionFit: Canines are the pointed eye-teeth.

clue.text: Horsemen surround a group of marauders

indicators.note: horsemen surrounding means their letters wrap around the single letter

parts.note: riders are horsemen

explanation.surface: Cavalry encircling a band of plunderers.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text lost the little word 'a'; with it restored, the cavalry wrap round that single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiders are attackers who plunder, a band of looters.

clue.text: Pardon for Amy when she comes round home

indicators.note: Amy coming round means her name is wrapped around the word for home

parts.note: a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A plea for clemency for Amy when she regains consciousness at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For', 'when' and 'she' are links; Amy's name is split after its second letter to admit the home.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to offenders.

clue.text: This lady may be about north of Nassau

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A woman who might be somewhere just north of the Bahamian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges NNASSAU. 'May be' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as in the Apocrypha story of Susanna and the Elders.
